chunks: One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Salih al-Taymuli, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! With me is the most highly dowered of the Arabs, and I would love for you to accept her, and she is my daughter.' He said, 'I have accepted her.' He said, 'So (there is) another, O Messenger of Allah!' He said, 'And what is she?' He said, 'Hardship has not struck her forehead at all.' He said, 'There is no need for me regarding her, but marry her to Jilbeeb.'

So the legs of the man failed from what entered into him. Then he went to her mother and informed her of the news, so what entered her was similar to what had entered him. So the girl heard his speech and saw what had entered her father, so she said to them, 'Be pleased for me with whatever Allah and His Messenger are pleased with for me.'

So that consoled both of them, and her father came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and informed him of the news. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'I have made her dowry to be Paradise.'
And Safwan added in it, saying, 'So Jilbeeb died from her, and her dowry reached one hundred thousand dirhams after him.'

key_terms.مَهِيرَةُ الْعَرَبِ: The most highly dowered of the Arabs

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the Prophet's daughter or the highly dowered woman who was married to Jilbeeb?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) discernment in marriage, rejecting a wealthy but potentially unsuitable match in favor of Jilbeeb, whose name implies nobility or piety. The daughter’s acceptance of her father’s choice with the phrase 'Be pleased with what Allah and His Messenger are pleased with' highlights the Shia emphasis on *rida* (contentment) with divine decree in familial matters. The concluding statement that her *mahr* (dowry) became Paradise underscores the spiritual valuation of marital compatibility over material wealth.
